name: braided adjacency tide
algorithm: Parse the inscription into Unicode grapheme clusters. Build a directed multigraph whose vertices are cluster positions and whose edges join consecutive positions. For each round r from 0 through 5, compute a stable ordering by sorting vertices on (outdegree - indegree, (position + r) mod n, position). Re-emit clusters by alternating the first unused vertex from the front and back of that ordering; after each emission, redirect every edge incident to the emitted vertex to the next vertex in cyclic order. Preserve cluster identity and multiplicity. Apply the six rounds to the whole sequence, then insert a separator glyph at every edge whose direction reversed an odd number of times.
intended_pressure: Stress whether adjacency can remain legible when local neighbors are repeatedly reselected by a global degree balance.

name: nested phase membrane
algorithm: Tokenize into grapheme clusters and assign each token depth 0. Repeatedly scan left to right with a stack: on an opening glyph, increase depth; on a closing glyph, decrease depth but never below zero; on any other glyph, rotate it left by depth modulo its code-point count. Replace every maximal run at equal depth by a node containing its reversed children. Perform four bottom-up passes: concatenate child strings in order on even passes and in reverse order on odd passes, then rotate each node by its depth plus pass index. Add a new opening or closing glyph according to the node's parity (length modulo 2). Serialize depth-first, retaining all original tokens.
intended_pressure: Stress hierarchical reading by making nesting depth alter both token interiors and the order in which enclosing membranes resolve.

name: countercurrent phoneme loom
algorithm: Partition grapheme clusters into three lanes using position modulo 3. In each lane, encode every cluster as its Unicode code-point sequence. For round r from 0 through 7, sort lane A ascending by code-point sum, lane B descending by (sum, length), and lane C by a stable rotation of (length, first code point). Zip the lanes using a direction pattern [A,B,C,C,B,A] repeated, taking one item from each selected lane and reversing the code-point sequence when its lane is selected on a descending step. Between zipped items emit a marker whose code point is (sum of the three item sums + r) modulo the marker table length. Decode code points back to glyphs after the final round.

name: anti-causal rewrite spiral
algorithm: Represent the inscription as a list of grapheme clusters and a cursor initially at 0. For round r from 1 through 9, create a fresh list by visiting indices in the order generated by modular stepping: start=(cursor+r) mod n, step=2r+1; if step and n share a factor, replace step with the least larger coprime integer. At each visited index, emit the token transformed by a permutation of its code points chosen from a four-state cycle (identity, reverse, rotate-left, rotate-right), where the state is (r + index + previous emitted code-point sum) mod 4. Set cursor to the final visited index. After each round, splice a duplicate of every token whose transformed sum is prime, immediately before its next occurrence in the visit order. Stop if length exceeds 4096; otherwise continue all rounds.
